sections.doc: who is let in (the user guide's "Who can reach your server": its setups) Each listed network (CIDR) says what a request from it gets: trusted, authenticated or refused; the longest prefix holding the client's address decides, and a request from no listed network is refused too (403). The server does not start when an address of server.host can be reached from a network no list covers, or only from an authenticated one while api-key is empty; nor when server.host lists a wildcard beside another address, or one address twice; nor when public-url is https, loopback is trusted and no proxy network covers it. Every request must name the server by one of its own host names (421 otherwise), and a change sent by another site's page is refused (403).

fields.doc: The networks a reverse proxy connects from: ["127.0.0.0/8", "::1/128"] for one on this machine, a load balancer's address or network for one elsewhere; empty, no proxy. A request that carries Forwarded, X-Forwarded-For, X-Forwarded-Host, X-Forwarded-Proto, X-Real-IP or Via came through a proxy. From a peer in these networks it is the proxy's, so it needs api-key like an authenticated network's (the proxy must set one of those headers on every request); from any other peer it is refused (403) whatever it carries. A proxy network lets nothing in by itself: its peers must also be in trusted- or authenticated-networks. Required to cover loopback when public-url is https and loopback is trusted.

THE CENTRAL SCHEDULER (docs/research-goal-advancement.md "As built"): one decision per managers' tick about which pending manager item starts a run, across every job type.
